hypothesis: Fast EMA above slow EMA on 5-minute bars predicts positive return
mechanism: Slow diffusion of information and trend-following flows; expected weak intraday, used to calibrate the pipeline
hold_profile: 30-120 min, low win rate, large winners

hypothesis: Break of the trailing 60-minute high (low) predicts continuation
mechanism: Stops clustered beyond recent range get triggered, pushing price further; breakout traders pile in

hypothesis: Prior session's close-to-close return predicts today's 8:30-15:00 CT return
mechanism: Time-series momentum at the shortest horizon; MOP find it at 1-12 months, so a daily version is expected to be weak or reverse
hold_profile: intraday hold, one trade a day

hypothesis: First half-hour return (8:30-9:00 CT) predicts last half-hour return (14:30-15:00 CT)
mechanism: Late informed trading and end-of-day rebalancing in the direction of the day's news (Gao et al.); dealer gamma hedging (Baltussen et al.)
hold_profile: 30 min, one trade a day, finishes before 3:10 PM

hypothesis: Rest-of-day return (prior close to 14:30 CT) predicts last half-hour return
mechanism: Option market makers short gamma hedge in the direction of the move late in the day (Baltussen et al. rROD)
result: ES IC +0.044 t 2.36; NQ IC +0.025 t 1.34; strong only in high-vol tercile (see IMOM-04)

hypothesis: Overnight return plus first half-hour return predicts last half-hour return
mechanism: Overnight news is absorbed by investors who trade late (Gao et al. ONFH variant)

hypothesis: IMOM-02 is stronger on high-volatility, down-trending days (proxy for negative dealer gamma)
mechanism: Without option data we proxy negative gamma by elevated realized vol and a falling market; momentum should appear only then
kill: no difference in IC between proxy states (|t|<2)
result: Stage 1 robust in dev (t 3.2-4.4 over cut-offs and leave-one-year-out). Strategy (MNQ 14:30-15:00): dev $3.75-4.18/trade, Combine pass <=43% in-sample. Walk-forward Nov 2024-Oct 2025: $-38/trade t -2.32 (no stop), $-17 t -1.71 (stop). KILLED iter 2.

hypothesis: Direction of the first 5-minute bar after 8:30 CT predicts the rest of the session (5-minute opening-range breakout, stop at far side of the bar)
mechanism: Opening auction resolves overnight disagreement; early order flow carries information; stop-out of losers is quick
kill: net expectancy <= 0 at single cost (replication found ~0 net on NQ)
hold_profile: to close, ~25% win rate, rare large winners: poor fit for 150+ days
result: NQ IC +0.071 t 3.90 PASS; P&L 1.50 pts/trade t 0.91, 2.2x NQ cost, fails MNQ; negative 2021-2024. ES IC +0.048 t 2.59 FAIL

hypothesis: Break of the 30-minute opening range predicts continuation to the close
mechanism: Same as IMOM-05 with a wider, less noisy range

hypothesis: NQ return over the last 1-5 minutes predicts ES return over the next 1-5 minutes (and the reverse)
mechanism: Information about tech-heavy news reaches NQ first; arbitrageurs align ES with a lag
kill: default; also fails if peak IC is below 1 minute (untradable from home)

hypothesis: Mega-cap stock moves (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA) lead NQ at 1-5 minutes
mechanism: Single-stock news hits the stock before index arbitrage moves futures; Hasbrouck predicts the reverse (futures lead), so expected to fail

hypothesis: VIX futures changes lead ES returns with a negative sign at 1-15 minutes
mechanism: Option hedgers buy volatility before selling futures

hypothesis: 10-year Treasury futures (ZN) moves lead ES at 1-15 minutes on macro-release days
mechanism: Rates react first to macro surprises; equity repricing follows; sign depends on the stock-bond correlation regime

hypothesis: A large z-score of the beta-hedged NQ/ES log-price spread (rolling 60 min) reverts within the session
mechanism: Both track overlapping large-cap baskets; temporary dislocations from one-sided flow are arbitraged away
kill: default; also fails cost test because two legs double costs
hold_profile: 15-60 min, high win rate, small wins: good fit

hypothesis: NQ outperforming ES over the morning predicts further NQ outperformance (risk-on continuation)
mechanism: Competes with RV-01: sector rotation flows persist through the day

hypothesis: An ES move not confirmed by RTY and YM over 15 minutes reverts
mechanism: Narrow, mega-cap-led moves lack broad buying and fade

hypothesis: Distance of price from session VWAP (in ATR units) reverts, mainly in low-volatility regimes
mechanism: Liquidity providers fade temporary impact; VWAP is the benchmark for institutional execution, so flow clusters around it
kill: default; also fails if IC in low-vol tercile is not larger than in high-vol
hold_profile: 15-60 min, high win rate: good fit

hypothesis: First touch of the overnight (Globex) high or low during the 8:30-10:00 CT window reverts
mechanism: Overnight extremes mark where thin-liquidity moves stopped; day-session participants fade them

hypothesis: The opening gap (8:30 CT open vs prior 15:00 CT close) partly fills in the first 90 minutes
mechanism: Overnight moves on thin volume overshoot; day-session liquidity corrects them

hypothesis: An extreme 5-minute return (|z|>2 vs time-of-day volatility) reverts over the next 15 minutes
mechanism: Price impact of a large order is partly transient (propagator model)

hypothesis: Prior day's high, low and close act as reversal levels on first touch
mechanism: Folklore; weak mechanism (resting orders at visible levels)

hypothesis: Aggressor-signed volume imbalance over the last 1-5 minutes predicts the next 1-15 minute return
mechanism: Persistent metaorders are split into many child orders, so buying pressure continues
kill: default; also fails if IC peaks below 1 minute

hypothesis: Best-level order-flow imbalance (Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov) aggregated to 1 minute predicts the next minute
mechanism: OFI explains contemporaneous price change; the predictive part comes from persistence of OFI itself

hypothesis: Micro-price minus mid predicts the next mid change
mechanism: Queue imbalance at the touch shows which side is about to be depleted
kill: IC at >=10 s below 0.01 (then L1/L2 microstructure is out of reach for a home bot)
hold_profile: seconds: tests the Level 1 vs Level 2 claim, not expected to be tradable

hypothesis: Direction of large single prints (top 1% by size) predicts continuation over 5-15 minutes
mechanism: Large aggressive orders are more likely informed

hypothesis: Multi-level OFI (levels 1-10) adds predictive power beyond best-level OFI at horizons of 10 s or longer
mechanism: Deeper orders reveal intentions not yet at the touch
kill: no significant incremental coefficient over OFI-02; gated: test only if OFI-01 or OFI-02 passes

hypothesis: Static depth imbalance (bid vs ask size, levels 1-5) predicts the next 1-minute return
mechanism: Thin side of the book is easier to push through

hypothesis: High VPIN predicts higher volatility in the next 30-60 minutes (filter, not direction)
mechanism: Informed, one-sided flow drives market makers to widen and withdraw
kill: VPIN adds nothing to trailing realized volatility in predicting future volatility (Andersen-Bondarenko critique)

hypothesis: Bulk-volume-classified imbalance over volume buckets predicts direction
mechanism: Same as OFI-01 measured in volume time

hypothesis: Trailing 20-day realized volatility regime decides whether momentum (high vol) or mean reversion (low vol) features work
mechanism: Gamma hedging and liquidity provision behave differently across volatility regimes
kill: IC of IMOM and MR features does not differ across vol terciles

hypothesis: A compressed overnight range relative to ATR predicts a larger day-session range
mechanism: Volatility clusters but also mean-reverts; quiet overnight sessions precede expansion
kill: no relation between overnight range ratio and day range (|t|<3)

hypothesis: Normalizing returns and signals by the time-of-day volatility profile improves IC stability
mechanism: Intraday volatility is U-shaped; raw thresholds fire too often at the open and too rarely at midday
kill: no improvement in IC stability across time buckets

hypothesis: Range-based volatility (Garman-Klass) is a better stop-scaling input than close-to-close volatility
mechanism: Range estimators use more of the bar and are more efficient
kill: no improvement in stop placement (MAE fit) over ATR

hypothesis: ES drifts up from the morning of a scheduled FOMC day to the 1:00 PM CT announcement
mechanism: Uncertainty resolution premium documented by Lucca and Moench; may have weakened after 2011
kill: mean return in 2015-2024 not positive; too few events (about 8 a year) for |t|>=3 means report only, no strategy

hypothesis: Scheduled macro releases (CPI, NFP, FOMC) change volatility and break other signals around the release
mechanism: Information shocks dominate any microstructure signal
kill: no difference in signal IC or volatility inside vs outside event windows

hypothesis: Turn-of-the-month days (last 1 and first 3 trading days) have higher intraday drift
mechanism: Pension and payroll inflows

hypothesis: Monthly options expiration days show stronger mean reversion near large open-interest strikes
mechanism: Dealer hedging pins price near strikes
